title: Evodiamine rescues lipopolysaccharide-induced cognitive impairment via C/EBP-beta-COX2 axis-regulated neuroinflammation.
authors: Yang, Chunqi; Wu, Xiangjun; Jiang, Ziyu; Ru, Yi; Shen, Baoying; Li, Fangyang; Cui, Jialu; Zhang, Cheng; Wang, Xiaoqiang; Yu, Wenrun; Li, Yina; Huang, Ying; Kong, Ao; Hao, Feiran; Xiao, Chengrong; Wang, Yuguang; Gao, Yue
one_liner_zh: 该文研究中药成分吴茱萸碱通过C/EBP-beta-COX2轴缓解神经炎症，虽含分子对接与动力学模拟，但对象为小分子-蛋白互作而非蛋白质-DNA互作，与本课题TF-DNA结合机制关联较弱。
abstract: Neuroinflammation is a key driver of neurological disorders. Evodiamine (EVO), an alkaloid from the traditional Chinese herb Evodia rutaecarpa, possesses potent biological activities, notably anticancer and anti-inflammatory effects. This study investigates EVO's potential to attenuate LPS-induced neuroinflammation, focusing on identifying its therapeutic targets and mechanisms of action. EVO treatment significantly improved mitochondrial function and reduced oxidative stress in LPS-stimulated BV(2) cells, while also lowering levels of pro-inflammatory factors (IL-6, NO, IL-1beta) in brain organoids. In mice, EVO treatment alleviated behavioral abnormalities, especially in cognition and memory, and lowered hippocampal inflammation marker levels. To elucidate the critical mechanisms by which EVO exerts its anti-inflammatory effects, we analyzed LPS-induced inflammatory injury in BV(2) cells and used transcriptomics to investigate whether EVO modulates the C/EBP-beta signaling pathway. Further validation using si-C/EBP-beta confirmed EVO's regulatory effect on the C/EBP-beta-COX2 axis, showing that knockdown significantly reduced pro-inflammatory factor expression, thereby providing neuroprotection. Moreover, molecular docking and dynamics simulations confirmed a stable interaction between EVO and C/EBP-beta, supporting its role in attenuating LPS-induced neuroinflammation. In summary, these findings suggest that EVO regulates inflammation-related pathways by targeting the C/EBP-beta-COX2 axis, offering neuroprotective benefits and mitigating neuroinflammatory responses.
abstract_zh: 神经炎症是神经系统疾病的关键驱动因素。吴茱萸碱（EVO）是从传统中草药吴茱萸（Evodia rutaecarpa）中提取的一种生物碱，具有强大的生物活性，尤其是抗癌和抗炎作用。本研究探讨EVO减轻脂多糖（LPS）诱导的神经炎症的潜力，重点在于识别其治疗靶点和作用机制。EVO处理显著改善了LPS刺激的BV(2)细胞中的线粒体功能并减少了氧化应激，同时降低了脑类器官中促炎因子（IL-6、NO、IL-1β）的水平。在小鼠中，EVO处理缓解了行为异常，尤其是在认知和记忆方面，并降低了海马区炎症标志物水平。为阐明EVO发挥抗炎作用的关键机制，我们分析了LPS诱导的BV(2)细胞炎症损伤，并利用转录组学研究了EVO是否调节C/EBP-β信号通路。进一步使用si-C/EBP-β进行验证，确认了EVO对C/EBP-β-COX2轴的调节作用，表明敲低显著降低了促炎因子的表达，从而提供神经保护。此外，分子对接和动力学模拟证实了EVO与C/EBP-β之间的稳定相互作用，支持其在减轻LPS诱导的神经炎症中的作用。总之，这些发现表明EVO通过靶向C/EBP-β-COX2轴调节炎症相关通路，提供神经保护益处并减轻神经炎症反应。
